title: secret create --replace leaves a duplicate entry when the driver no longer has the old secret
body:
### Issue Description

If the driver has lost the data of an existing secret (for example the `file` driver with `path=` on a tmpfs after a reboot), `podman secret create --replace` doesn't remove the old entry. It adds a second secret with the same name, and the old one can't be removed with `podman secret rm` either (that part is #27666).

It looks like `Store()` in `common/pkg/secrets/secrets.go` ignores `ErrNoSuchSecret` from `driver.Delete()` but then also skips `s.delete()`, so the old ID stays in the metadata.

### Steps to reproduce the issue

With a throwaway store:

```sh
W=$(mktemp -d); mkdir "$W/run"
pm() { podman --root "$W/root" --runroot "$W/runroot" --tmpdir "$W/tmp" "$@"; }
echo one | pm secret create --driver file --driver-opts path="$W/run" app.token -
rm "$W/run/secretsdata.json"   # driver data gone, like a tmpfs after a reboot
echo two | pm secret create --replace --driver file --driver-opts path="$W/run" app.token -
pm secret ls
```

### Describe the results you received

Two secrets named `app.token`:

```
ID                         NAME        DRIVER
1a6ace66bd6aeba56013c636a  app.token   file
e3ef853e98d6a2e1fbec10a95  app.token   file
```

`pm secret rm e3ef853e98d6a2e1fbec10a95` fails with `no such secret` and the entry stays. Each further `--replace` adds one more.

### Describe the results you expected

One `app.token` entry. When the driver says the old data is already gone, `--replace` should still drop the old metadata. Other driver errors should still fail as they do today.

### podman info output

```yaml
podman 6.2.0 (podman-6.2.0-1.fc45, containers-common-0.70.0-1.fc45), Fedora 45, amd64
Also reproduced with podman 5.7.0 on Ubuntu 26.04.
```

### Podman in a container

Yes

### Privileged Or Rootless

Rootless

### Upstream Latest Release

Yes

### Additional environment details

6.2.0 ran inside a Fedora 45 container, 5.7.0 directly on the host.

### Additional information

podman-container-tools/container-libs#558 fixes the `rm` side of #27666 but doesn't touch `--replace`. #27130 covers `--replace` on a name that doesn't exist yet.

comments.body:
Hi! I'd like to work on this issue.

I looked through the issue description, and the problem seems to be in `Store()` in `common/pkg/secrets/secrets.go`. When `driver.Delete()` returns `ErrNoSuchSecret`, the error is ignored, but the old entry is not removed from the metadata store. As a result, `--replace` creates a new secret while leaving the old one behind.

I'd like to look into the existing deletion logic and fix it so that the old metadata is removed even when the driver has already lost the secret data. At the same time, other driver errors should still be handled as before.

I'll also add a regression test covering this scenario and check that the existing `--replace` behavior is not affected.

I'd be happy to work on this and submit a PR to container-libs (i' ve already read CONTRIBUTING.md btw). Could you assign it to me?
